original_question: Is there a Riemannian metric on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 whose geodesic flow has zero Liouville entropy?
target_in_paper: Question 10.1.2 (Paternain) in §10.1: "Is there a Riemannian metric on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 whose geodesic flow has zero Liouville entropy?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official target almost verbatim. It has the correct category of structure (Riemannian metric), the correct ambient manifold class (closed surface of genus ≥ 2), and the correct dynamical property (the geodesic flow having zero Liouville entropy).
missing_details: To make it fully stand-alone, specify that the geodesic flow is the flow φ_t on the unit tangent bundle SM, in the notation of §1.
Unpack 'Liouville entropy' as the metric entropy of φ_t with respect to the Liouville measure on SM.
Make explicit that the surface is closed and connected; the paper's standing notation assumes connected C∞ manifolds.

For paper-faithful context, note that this question is presented as an easier version of Question 10.1.1 on complete integrability, motivated by Mañé's result that Hamiltonian flows on surfaces are generically Anosov or have zero Liouville exponents.
Do not broaden the problem to Finsler metrics: Question 10.1.3 is only a special case of a Finsler analogue, not the main target here.
refined_question: Does there exist a smooth Riemannian metric g on a closed connected surface M of genus at least 2 such that the geodesic flow φ_t on the unit tangent bundle SM has zero metric entropy with respect to the Liouville measure?
justification: The draft is targeting §10.1 exactly, and more specifically Question 10.1.2, not a neighboring problem from §6 about nonpositive curvature or ergodicity. The immediately preceding Question 10.1.1 shows that the paper frames this as an easier version of the complete-integrability problem, and the sentence citing Mañé gives the intended motivation. Section 1 supplies the paper's ambient notation for the geodesic flow on SM. Question 10.1.3 should not replace the target, because the paper presents it only as a special case of a Finsler analogue of Question 10.1.2.
